text: A ROS node that carries out long-running tasks on request and reports feedback and a result. For navigation, the request may be a position. The feedback may be the time spent navigating and the distance to the goal, and the result is a boolean for success.

evidence.quote: For navigation, the request may be a position.
The feedback may be the time spent navigating and the distance to the goal, and the result is a boolean for success.

text: A collision object that has been fixed to a robot link in the planning scene moves with the tool. It is checked for collisions as part of the robot. When it is attached, RViz draws it in a different color.

evidence.quote: when it is attached, RViz draws it in a different color and it moves with the tool.

text: The Nav2 server that runs the behavior tree and calls the planner, controller and behavior servers. Node plugins are assembled into a tree inside the BT Navigator, and the tree itself is read from an XML file.

evidence.quote: Node plugins are assembled into a tree inside the BT Navigator, and the tree itself is read from an XML file.

text: The computer that runs the robot's program decides what to do next. It ranges from a small microcontroller like an Arduino to an industrial robot controller.
The list in an ament_python package's setup.py tells the build which extra files to copy into the install space. It lists files such as launch and YAML files.
A Universal Robots add-on lets ROS command the robot arm. When its node runs in a pendant program, it fetches a URScript program from the ROS driver on the PC and runs it.

A 3D robot simulator with physics simulates a robot, its sensors and its surroundings. It connects to ROS 2 so code can be tested before running on real hardware. Each ROS 2 release has a matching Gazebo version.

evidence.quote: Gazebo is the usual simulator for ROS, and each ROS 2 release has a matching Gazebo version.

text: A color representation separating image data into hue (color type), saturation (color purity), and value (brightness) channels. In OpenCV HSV color space, the hue channel spans from 0 to 179 while saturation and value span from 0 to 255.

evidence.quote: In OpenCV HSV color space, the hue channel spans from 0 to 179 while saturation and value span from 0 to 255.

text: The component of a PID controller that integrates past tracking errors over time eliminates residual steady-state droop. Even a tiny steady-state error that persists makes the integral grow, which increases the control output until the error reaches zero.

evidence.quote: Even a tiny steady-state error that persists makes the integral grow, which increases the control output until the error reaches zero.

text: The proprietary, Pascal-like programming language (KUKA Robot Language) used to program KUKA industrial manipulators. Keeping data apart from logic means a taught point can be changed without editing the motion code.

evidence.quote: Keeping data apart from logic means a taught point can be changed without editing the motion code.

text: A robot that moves through its environment instead of staying bolted in place relies on sensors to map, localize and plan paths. These include machines such as a warehouse robot or planetary rover.

A MoveIt 2 library (MTC) breaks a manipulation job such as pick and place into a chain of stages that are planned together. These stages can be inspected one by one in RViz. MTC splits a task into stages of three kinds.

evidence.quote: MTC splits a task into stages of three kinds.

text: The Nav2 action a client uses to ask the robot to drive to a pose. For navigation, the request may be a position. The feedback may be the time spent navigating and the distance to the goal, and the result is a boolean for success.

evidence.quote: For navigation, the request may be a position.
The feedback may be the time spent navigating and the distance to the goal, and the result is a boolean for success.

text: A RAPID function returns a copy of a robtarget moved by given X, Y and Z distances in millimeters. The offset is applied in the coordinate system of the work object.

evidence.quote: The offset is applied in the coordinate system of the work object.

text: An exchange of latched request and acknowledge signals between a PLC and a robot lets each know the other's state. These include signals such as cycle-start, busy and done.

The component of a PID controller generates output directly proportional to the current instantaneous tracking error. As the robot approaches the setpoint, the error shrinks toward zero. The proportional push becomes too weak to overcome opposing physical forces such as gearbox friction or gravity.

evidence.quote: As the robot approaches the setpoint, the error shrinks toward zero
the proportional push becomes too weak to overcome opposing physical forces such as gearbox friction or gravity.

text: A named block of ABB RAPID code starts with MODULE and ends with ENDMODULE. Inside, data declarations come at the top, followed by routines such as PROC, FUNC and TRAP.
An ABB RAPID function shifts a target along the axes of the tool. It is often used to compute approach and retract points from a grip point.
An ABB RAPID data type defines a complete robot position in millimeters and tool orientation as a quaternion. It also includes arm axis configurations and external axis positions.
A device that measures the robot or its surroundings includes instruments such as an encoder, an ultrasonic range finder or a camera. It is the "sense" part of the sense, think, act loop.

A DC circuit configuration that gives a path to supply common (-). Sinking field devices use NPN transistor outputs and sourcing field devices use PNP outputs. An NPN sinking field device requires a PLC I/O module with a sourcing input.

evidence.quote: Sinking field devices use NPN transistor outputs and sourcing field devices use PNP outputs.
An NPN sinking field device requires a PLC I/O module with a sourcing input.

text: A DC circuit configuration that gives a path to supply source (+). A sourcing circuit connects the positive supply rail to the load, driving conventional current out through the terminal.

evidence.quote: A sourcing circuit connects the positive supply rail to the load, driving conventional current out through the terminal.

text: Consistent odometry errors caused by physical robot imperfections, such as unequal wheel diameters or wheelbase uncertainty, repeat identically across runs. They can be measured and corrected by software calibration.

evidence.quote: so they can be measured and corrected in software.

text: A message_filters synchronization utility that aligns multiple incoming ROS 2 topic streams by matching their header timestamps. This synchronization guarantees that image frames are never processed with stale or misaligned calibration metadata.

evidence.quote: This synchronization guarantees that image frames are never processed with stale or misaligned calibration metadata.

text: A named, unidirectional communication channel in ROS over which nodes publish and subscribe to continuous data streams. A topic can have zero or more publishers and zero or more subscribers, and every subscriber receives the data published by any publisher.

evidence.quote: A topic can have zero or more publishers and zero or more subscribers, and every subscriber receives the data published by any publisher.

text: An XML file (Unified Robot Description Format) describes a robot as a tree of links joined by joints. For each joint, it specifies its type, axis, position and limits.
A coordinate frame attached to a fixture or workpiece serves as a reference that program targets are measured from. Re-teaching this frame moves all targets without changing the program.
How to choose and size grippers, mount them and set payload. It shows how to program the digital I/O that opens a gripper, confirms a grip and talks to a PLC, in URScript and RAPID.

How robots turn a target into smooth setpoints with trapezoidal, triangular and S-curve profiles. It covers cubic and quintic time scaling, joint, linear and circular interpolation, zones, and time parameterization in MoveIt.

3D perception for robotics: direct sensing versus 2D inference, stereo disparity geometry, and point cloud filtering with PCL (PassThrough, VoxelGrid, outliers). It also covers RANSAC planes, Euclidean clustering, and bin picking.
Capstone project: build a pick-and-place task for a simulated UR5e with ROS 2, MoveIt 2 and the MoveIt Task Constructor. It runs on mock hardware or Gazebo, with milestones, tests and a rubric.
